brief.title: Agents calling agents: follow the chain
brief.why: Tuesday is how-it-works. The last three posts were a feature (Ledger), a release (v0.2.11) and a take; agent-to-agent delegation is a documented, engineer-shaped mechanism (signed tokens, on-behalf-of gates) we haven't explained yet, and it's a real permission gap people hit as they chain agents.

linkedin.text:
Your support bot can't touch the finance tools. Can the research agent it calls?

That's the gap with agents calling agents. Each agent has its own key and its own permissions, so a public-facing bot with narrow access can ask a more privileged agent to do what it was never allowed to do itself.

How Control Tower closes it:

1. support-bot calls research-agent through an MCP tool (or an HTTP API, or A2A). On the way, Control Tower hands research-agent a signed delegation token.
2. research-agent sends that token back as an x-ct-delegation header on its own model and tool calls.
3. Every one of those calls is now recorded as made for support-bot, and a gate can match on it: on_behalf_of: [team:support], servers: [ledger], effect: deny. Anywhere up the chain.

Mark the called agent's key as acting only on behalf of others and calls without a valid token are refused, so leaving the token off doesn't get around the gate.

The rest is plumbing you'd want anyway: A calls B calls A is refused as a loop, chains stop at 8 agents deep, tokens expire after 15 minutes, and what research-agent spends for support-bot counts against support-bot's budget too.

Open source and self-hosted. A ⭐ helps others find it:
https://github.com/joshmaster2165/controltower

#AIAgents #MCP #OpenSource
linkedin.document_title: Agents calling agents: who are they acting for?

posts:
Your support bot can't touch the finance tools.

But it can ask the research agent, which can.

Agents calling agents is where per-agent permissions quietly stop meaning anything. Here's how Control Tower follows the chain:

When one agent calls another through Control Tower (an MCP tool, an HTTP API or A2A), the called agent gets a signed delegation token.

It sends it back as x-ct-delegation on its own calls, and each of those is recorded as made for the caller.

So a gate can match whom a call is for, anywhere up the chain:

on_behalf_of: [team:support] → deny ledger

Keys that act only for others are refused without a valid token. Loops are refused, chains stop at 8 deep, tokens expire in 15 min.

Open-source, self-hosted AI gateway for agents, models and MCP tools. A star helps the next platform team find it:
https://github.com/joshmaster2165/controltower

brief.notes: All mechanics from docs/agent-to-agent.md (delegation token, x-ct-delegation, delegated_only keys, on_behalf_of gates, delegation_loop, 8-deep limit, 15-minute expiry, never logged, spend counted against both budgets). Agent names are the doc's own examples, not customers.
